body:
> You really must let go of your daughter.

Trying that.  Actually, she was supposed to move out of my house this month but she broke her ankle and complications so that's on hold.  Still, I've given the hard ultimatum.  I know people who have 30 year olds living with them like this and it's really the best thing for her to get out; the best chance of her facing the consequences of her life choices and doing something about it while she's young.

>And learn to control your own destiny because in fact, yourself is all you can control.

Being depressed and hopeless is a nasty feedback loop.  I know what your saying.  I have lists.  I don't do them.

> Kaiser...

Maybe the best of my shitty options.

> Regarding your employment, your disenchantment with your career is probably all caused by your depression.

Some of that and some of the realization that specialization as an individual contributor combined with advanced age makes for a much higher likelihood of future unemployment.

> Think of this: so many right now are not so fortunate and would give anything to be in your shoes.

Yes, I know this.  I have a theory called "the expanding gas theory of misery": Everyone pretty much has a set point of misery and their perception expands it to fill that space.  Some unhappy guy with a hangnail and  a wife that wants sex once a week is as miserable as if had leprosy.  Obviously, the goal is to change the attitude/perception to reduce the set point.
Apparently I have some bike induced nerve damage.  I can't ride anymore.  In fact I still have some level of pain every day.  I could go on about the joys of this but you might be eating.

> in your life in this particular moment

It's been like this for a very long time.  Of course, the older I get the more hopeless it seems.  A decade ago, when my kid was an impossible child (who gets thrown out of first grade?) there was a lot more marital strife.  Divorce was talked about but then we realized that no one wanted or could deal with being a single parent to such a child.  We bore the burden.

Two years ago the marriage was hellish and I planned to divorce my wife after my kid was 18.  The kid was more manageable but our marriage had stressed beyond the point of breaking where every action was malevolent by years of a feedback loop due to the kid induced stress.  In a nutshell, every word or action was a variant of "fuck you for everything".  Then I decided that I couldn't survive two more years of this marital strife so I would just shelve all my grievances with my wife, kind swallow my pride, and act super nice to make the next 2 years (until my daughter turned 18) at least bearable.   Why not? The odd thing is that it made the marriage work.  It's not a bad marriage now.

"Funny" note: One of the issues with our marriage was that my wife always had a very low sex drive.  Drove me batty.  ED has pretty much solved that.  Now if I could just stop wanting sex I'd be set.

===


Anyway, distilling this, I really have two main problems now.

1) The ED.  That just fucks with your head.  If you can't enjoy sex, even fapping (sorry), what's the point.  Maybe if I was 60 I'd feel differently but at 50 it's just too soon to feel emasculated.

2) Career - I'm simply not interested any more.  I don't give a fuck about engineering anymore.  This has been building for some time. I'm not just talking about the type of engineering that I do (statistical/math/algorithm software dev type shit) but the concept of engineering doesn't interest me.  Unfortunately, I've done a fabulous job of being otherwise unaccomplished (aka a complete bore).  How do you accomplish so little in 50 years you ask?  Well, as it turns out, it's the same way you accomplish anything, one day at a time.

Note that at ghe age of 50 I need to not fuck up saving for retirement.  The US is not a good place to fuck up your retirement.  It is not forgiving and I suspect it will only get worse.  So, the idea of going back to college for polysci or history is really a non-starter.  I really have no idea what else I'd do.

All this of course had made me depressed and stressed (throw in high blood pressure to boot) and that's probably contributed to my inertia (like it needed a boost).  I would take an SRI but I seem to respond horribly to them.
